findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Name the target test file(s) for the new Cloud and DC create-path issuetype pin tests (e.g. `tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/adapters/jira/test_outbound_fields_type_pins.py` and `tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/adapters/jira_datacenter/test_backend_type_pins.py`, or an existing suite file) so the executor does not have to choose.
evidence: ABSENCE: no test file path is given for the new Cloud or DC create-path pin tests
"an assertion on the built `'issuetype'` field for each of `task`/`story`/`bug`/`epic` through the Cloud create path and through the DC create path" — content is specified but target file is not

findings.finding: The Testing section and Scope bullet specify that new characterization pin tests for both create paths are owned by this ticket, but neither section names the target test file(s) where those pins should be written. An executor must choose a file without guidance.
findings.location: Testing section — 'both create paths keep producing their current issue-type values, pinned BY VALUE'; Scope — 'the characterization pins for the type mapping on both create paths — this ticket owns them unconditionally'
scenarios: The executor creates a new file that conflicts with, or duplicates, the sibling story cedc's DC characterization suite, causing ownership confusion the plan tries to avoid by explicitly claiming these pins.

evidence: "re-add a literal … to `adapters/jira_datacenter/backend.py`, run the boundary-guard module, record that the new test is RED (and note the pass/fail counts), revert the mutation, record that it is GREEN again"

findings.finding: The mutation-check proving command is described as 'run the boundary-guard module' without a concrete invocation, leaving the executor to infer which pytest command (or module invocation) demonstrates the RED result.
findings.location: Testing section — 'run the boundary-guard module, record that the new test is RED'
scenarios: An executor who is unfamiliar with the test layout must discover the correct pytest -k filter or module path by inspection, introducing a stop-and-investigate step that the concreteness requirement is meant to eliminate.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Extend `test_both_cloud_callers_resolve_to_the_single_definition` (or add a parallel test) to assert `outbound_fields._LOCAL_TO_JIRA_TYPE is LOCAL_TYPE_TO_JIRA` and the DC backend equivalent, matching the J2 pattern that already covers STATUS and PRIORITY.
evidence: Plan Scope: 'tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/test_jira_family_boundary_heldout.py — extend the one-literal guard to the type map.' — names only the 'one-literal guard' extension, not the identity-check test.

Observed code at test_jira_family_boundary_heldout.py:314-326: `test_both_cloud_callers_resolve_to_the_single_definition` asserts `acli._LOCAL_STATUS_TO_JIRA is LOCAL_STATUS_TO_JIRA`, `acli._LOCAL_PRIORITY_TO_JIRA is LOCAL_PRIORITY_TO_JIRA`, `outbound_fields._LOCAL_TO_JIRA_STATUS is LOCAL_STATUS_TO_JIRA`, `outbound_fields._LOCAL_TO_JIRA_PRIORITY is LOCAL_PRIORITY_TO_JIRA` — no TYPE-map assertion.
The J2 pattern being followed added identity assertions here for STATUS and PRIORITY; TYPE is not covered and the plan does not mention this gap.
findings.finding: The plan's Scope and AC enumerate the boundary guard test file (`test_jira_family_boundary_heldout.py`) as requiring a new `test_exactly_one_type_map_literal_within_adapters` assertion, but never mentions that `test_both_cloud_callers_resolve_to_the_single_definition` (`:314`) must also be extended to assert TYPE-map identity. That test currently asserts identity only for STATUS and PRIORITY. The analogous identity assertion for `outbound_fields._LOCAL_TO_JIRA_TYPE is LOCAL_TYPE_TO_JIRA` (and the DC backend equivalent) is a concrete patch site the Scope omits.
findings.location: Scope section: 'tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/test_jira_family_boundary_heldout.py — extend the one-literal guard to the type map.'
scenarios: `test_both_cloud_callers_resolve_to_the_single_definition` will pass after the change even if outbound_fields._LOCAL_TO_JIRA_TYPE is a separate in-module object (not the imported canonical), because the test never checks TYPE identity — the 'proven by a single object' guarantee would be absent for TYPE while appearing complete by the test name.
The DC backend's `_LOCAL_TO_JIRA_TYPE` alias is also not covered by any identity assertion in the plan's test scope, leaving the DC create-path with no object-identity proof of single-sourcing.
findings.suggested_fix: Add to `test_both_cloud_callers_resolve_to_the_single_definition` (or a new sibling test): `from rebar_reconciler.adapters.jira_family import LOCAL_TYPE_TO_JIRA; assert outbound_fields._LOCAL_TO_JIRA_TYPE is LOCAL_TYPE_TO_JIRA; assert dc_backend._LOCAL_TO_JIRA_TYPE is LOCAL_TYPE_TO_JIRA`.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Tag each 'recorded in a comment' AC with `[operator-attested]` (or move the evidence into the repo — e.g., a code comment in `value_maps.py` recording the diff result, and a CI step that replays the mutation check) so that each has a concrete, rubric-compliant proving command.
evidence: "the two existing copies are DIFFED and the result is recorded in a comment on this ticket"
"if the two copies diverge, the chosen value is decided explicitly with its rationale recorded"
"that guard is MUTATION-CHECKED by the concrete procedure in Testing, with the RED and GREEN verdicts recorded in a comment"
ABSENCE: none of these bullets carries the `[operator-attested]` prefix required by the rubric's operator-attested rule
findings.finding: Three acceptance criteria use 'recorded in a comment on this ticket' as their sole proof of completion — (1) the diff result, (2) the divergence decision with rationale, and (3) the RED/GREEN mutation verdicts — but none carries the `[operator-attested]` tag. These ACs are not verifiable from repo artifacts, and without the tag the rubric does not treat a ticket-comment attestation as sufficient proving evidence.
findings.location: Acceptance criteria — first, second, and seventh bullets; Testing section (mutation-check RED/GREEN recording)
scenarios: A reviewer closing the PR cannot confirm from repo artifacts that the diff was performed, that a divergence was resolved, or that the mutation test was actually run — the work could be signed off without any of these steps having occurred.
If a future audit queries the repo, the record of key decisions (divergence resolution, mutation check) is in the ticket comment system, not in the codebase.
findings.suggested_fix: Prefix the three affected AC bullets with `[operator-attested]` so the rubric's attestation rule applies, and require the ticket comment to include a change-id or timestamp. Alternatively, encode the diff comparison as a code comment in `value_maps.py` (e.g. `# Copies were identical at unification; see PR <N>`) and make the mutation-check verdict a pytest --co dry-run output committed to a CI log artifact.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Add an explicit back-out / rollback plan (or expand-contract sequencing) for the case where the two copies are found to have diverged — 'decide and record' is necessary but not sufficient; describe how the behavioral change is safely deployed and reversed if needed.
evidence: 'If they have already drifted, the unification is a BEHAVIOUR change for one deployment and needs the divergence decided explicitly and recorded — the way J2 decided "deleted" -> "Done" — not silently resolved by whichever copy is moved.'
No expand-contract sequencing, staged rollout guidance, or back-out plan is described anywhere in the plan for the divergence scenario.
T4 checklist: 'The remedy is an explicit rollback/back-out plan or expand-contract — acknowledgement alone is insufficient.'
findings.finding: If the two copies of `_LOCAL_TO_JIRA_TYPE` have drifted, unifying them silently changes runtime behavior on one deployment path (Cloud or DC). The plan acknowledges this risk and requires the divergence to be 'decided explicitly with rationale recorded,' but provides no rollback/back-out plan or expand-contract sequencing for safely deploying a behavioral change to an already-running create path.
findings.location: Approach section ('Compare the two copies BEFORE unifying them'); AC items 1–2 ('the two existing copies are DIFFED'; 'if the two copies diverge, the chosen value is decided explicitly')
scenarios: Implementer discovers the Cloud copy has `"bug": "Bug"` and the DC copy has `"bug": "Defect"`. They pick one, merge, and deploy. DC create-path now silently creates a different issue type than before for all `bug`-typed tickets. There is no described rollback mechanism if this breaks downstream workflows.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a sub-section under Approach: 'If the copies diverge: (1) record the diff in a ticket comment; (2) deploy the unified value behind a feature flag or to a staging environment first; (3) rollback procedure is to revert the value_maps.py commit and re-deploy — note the revert SHA in the ticket.' Even a one-sentence rollback note ('revert the value_maps.py change and redeploy to restore prior behavior') satisfies T4.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Add `adapters/jira_family/__init__.py` as an explicit named file target in the Scope section (add `LOCAL_TYPE_TO_JIRA` to its import block and `__all__`), so the alias import resolves without relying on readers to infer the requirement from the parenthetical.
evidence: The current jira_family/__init__.py imports and re-exports LOCAL_STATUS_TO_JIRA and LOCAL_PRIORITY_TO_JIRA from value_maps (confirmed by file read lines 43-64), but LOCAL_TYPE_TO_JIRA is absent from both the import block and __all__.
The plan's alias import syntax `from rebar_reconciler.adapters.jira_family import LOCAL_TYPE_TO_JIRA as _LOCAL_TO_JIRA_TYPE` resolves through __init__.py, so __init__.py must be edited.

An implementer reading only the 5-bullet Scope list would not see __init__.py as a named edit target; the file is covered only by the parenthetical '(and its export from the package __init__...)' in the first bullet.
The J2 precedent (story 62d9) also required updating __init__.py's imports and __all__ when adding new symbols — this edit is load-bearing, not cosmetic.
findings.finding: `adapters/jira_family/__init__.py` is required to export `LOCAL_TYPE_TO_JIRA` for the alias import `from rebar_reconciler.adapters.jira_family import LOCAL_TYPE_TO_JIRA` to resolve, but it is not listed as a named file target in the Scope section's bullet list — it appears only parenthetically within the first bullet's prose.
findings.location: Scope section, first bullet: 'adapters/jira_family/value_maps.py — the single definition (and its export from the package __init__, matching how the status/priority maps are exposed)'
scenarios: Implementer adds LOCAL_TYPE_TO_JIRA to value_maps.py but does not update __init__.py; the alias import `from rebar_reconciler.adapters.jira_family import LOCAL_TYPE_TO_JIRA` raises ImportError, breaking both create paths.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a sixth Scope bullet: `adapters/jira_family/__init__.py` — add `LOCAL_TYPE_TO_JIRA` to the `from rebar_reconciler.adapters.jira_family.value_maps import (...)` block and to `__all__`, matching the pattern for `LOCAL_STATUS_TO_JIRA` and `LOCAL_PRIORITY_TO_JIRA` at lines 43-64.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Re-derive the full reference inventory for both `_LOCAL_TO_JIRA_TYPE` (old name) and `LOCAL_TYPE_TO_JIRA` (new canonical name) using `find_referencing_symbols` from the LSP/Serena, then separately grep for both name strings, to produce a symbol-graph-grounded inventory rather than a single-string grep.
evidence: Plan text: 'A repo-wide `git grep -n _LOCAL_TO_JIRA_TYPE` (string grep, not just a semantic reference search — the LSP does not see string/attribute access reliably) returns exactly seven sites, and the plan accounts for all of them.'
This is an explicit statement that inventory was produced by grep/hand-enumeration, which is the stated-method branch trigger independent of whether a missing site can be named.
findings.finding: The plan states its affected-file/call-site inventory for `_LOCAL_TO_JIRA_TYPE` was derived by `git grep -n _LOCAL_TO_JIRA_TYPE` — a hand-enumeration method. Grep finds only string occurrences of the exact historical name; it will not find references to the new canonical name `LOCAL_TYPE_TO_JIRA` once it is introduced (e.g., future import aliases or re-exports added to `jira_family/__init__.py`), and it cannot surface dynamic/attribute-access references that differ from the exact string.
findings.location: Context section: 'A repo-wide `git grep -n _LOCAL_TO_JIRA_TYPE`... returns exactly seven sites, and the plan accounts for all of them.'
scenarios: If `LOCAL_TYPE_TO_JIRA` is exported from `jira_family/__init__.py` (as the plan requires, matching the STATUS/PRIORITY pattern), any future consumer importing it under a different alias would not be caught by a grep for `_LOCAL_TO_JIRA_TYPE` — a silent omission in a future re-derivation of the same inventory.

The plan does not derive the inventory for the new canonical name `LOCAL_TYPE_TO_JIRA` at all; only the old name was grepped. If any call site imports the canonical name directly (e.g., in a new test), it would be missed.
findings.suggested_fix: Run `find_referencing_symbols` on `_LOCAL_TO_JIRA_TYPE` in both `outbound_fields.py` and `backend.py`, AND separately grep the full tree for both `_LOCAL_TO_JIRA_TYPE` and `LOCAL_TYPE_TO_JIRA` as strings. Reconcile the two result sets into the inventory.
